extracted.intended_audience: freelance feature writers pitching lifestyle and magazine editors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for composing feature-story pitches aimed at lifestyle and magazine editors, covering pitch format, story/newsworthiness elements, practical production considerations, audience fit, author credibility, and genre distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3-4 paragraphs — concise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the pitch brief and focused; convey the hook, why it matters, sources/approach, and author's ability succinctly. Avoid long, unfocused emails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story, not a topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Story, not a topic — angle, not subject
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch a specific story with an angle or narrative, not a general beat or broad subject. Editors want concrete storylines they can assign or buy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written in story tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Written in story tone — sample voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the pitch in a voice that demonstrates how the piece will read; include a sample of the narrative tone rather than a dry synopsis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailored to publication — read first, mimic style
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customize pitch to the outlet: read it first, match its tone, and explain why the story belongs there (section fit, reader interest). Generic pitches lower acceptance chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters — interesting people with names
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature stories should include identifiable, interesting people to anchor the narrative. Name them and indicate why they matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twists and turns — narrative tension
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that the story has surprises or developments that sustain reader interest; indicate likely narrative complications or reversals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspense — mystery to resolve
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate a question or mystery that the piece will resolve, creating forward momentum for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color — vivid scene-setting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate sensory, scene-based detail potential (settings, moments) that will make the feature immersive and visually rich.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beautiful writing — prose quality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors look for strong prose; the pitch should show tasteful, well-crafted sentences as evidence of the writer's voice and ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original angle — fills coverage hole
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the piece offers a new or under-covered perspective so it doesn't replicate existing coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique perspective — fresh take
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify what makes the writer's viewpoint distinctive and why readers will care about this particular framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual potential — photo opportunities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag opportunities for compelling photographs or visual elements; editors value pitches that suggest strong imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sidebar potential — packaged elements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note any easily packaged sidebars (lists, tips, short Q&As) that could accompany the feature and increase its editorial utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infographic angle — data visualization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, indicate data or findings that could be turned into charts or graphics to enhance the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio/video — multimedia
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention whether the story lends itself to audio or video elements, which can make it more attractive for multi-platform coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source list — who you'll interview
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise list of proposed interviewees or experts to show reporting feasibility and depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research backing — studies, data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite any relevant studies, data, or research that will substantiate the reporting and strengthen the pitch's credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed deadline — reliability signal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer a realistic timeline or deadline to indicate you can deliver on schedule; this signals professionalism and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue why the outlet's audience will care — demonstrate clear reader relevance or emotional pull.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlet coverage gap filled
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the piece occupies a niche or fills a gap in the publication's existing coverage, increasing its editorial value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone match
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the pitch's tone aligns with the publication's voice and audience expectations; mismatched tone reduces chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section fit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the most appropriate section or placement to help editors envision where the story will run.

rubrics_metrics.name: Past clips
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include relevant published work that shows you can deliver at the required level and on similar topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject expertise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note any professional or lived-experience expertise that gives you authority to cover the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reportorial capacity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate ability to report the story (contacts, access, familiarity with sources or documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling protagonist
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify a central figure whose arc will engage readers and humanize the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative arc — beginning, middle, end
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that the story has a clear progression and resolution; editors want a sense of structure and payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensory detail potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensory detail potential — sights, sounds, smells
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out moments or scenes that will allow vivid sensory description to bring the story to life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely peg OR evergreen relevance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either tie the piece to a current news hook or explain its enduring relevance if evergreen; state which applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterintuitive angle
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight an unexpected finding or frame that subverts conventional wisdom and provokes curiosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Universal theme — speaks to wider experience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the specific story connects to broader human themes so it resonates beyond niche interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique access
rubrics_metrics.description: Unique access — author can get the story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain special access the writer has (sources, locations, documents) that makes the reporting possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual storytelling potential
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe sequences or details that lend themselves to strong visual narrative or photo-driven storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader takeaway
rubrics_metrics.description: Reader takeaway — what will they learn/feel?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about what readers will know, feel, or do after reading; a clear takeaway strengthens a pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the piece offers actionable advice or practical benefits, state those clearly (tips, how-tos, resources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspirational value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the story aims to inspire, articulate the emotional arc and why readers will find it uplifting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautionary value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the piece serves as a warning or lesson, clarify the risks or pitfalls it will illuminate for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service/Utility Feature characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Service / Utility Feature — Practical advice; How-to focus; Reader benefits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These features prioritize actionable guidance and clear reader benefit; pitch should foreground usefulness and stepwise information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Feature characteristics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These pieces require strong reporting, scenes, and character development; pitch should emphasize story elements and scenes to be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trend Story characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Trend Story — Multiple examples of pattern; Why now?; Cultural significance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For trend pieces, show several representative examples, establish the pattern, and explain its timeliness and cultural import.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profile characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Profile — Single subject deeply explored; Defining moment / question; Why this person now?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profiles should center on a defining question or moment that reveals the subject's significance; explain access and narrative arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative Feature characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigative Feature — Wrongdoing or hidden truth; Document trail; Multiple sources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations need a document trail and corroborating sources; demonstrate evidence and reporting plan in the pitch.
